answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one licensed wind turbine on a named ridge, where a technician services its ferrous gearbox and threads a serial-numbered cable through the nacelle as a seal logged by the wind-farm operator. Random checks summon the holder to climb that turbine and read the cable serial on camera within hours, and one operator cannot climb two turbines at once. The service fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real turbine, another climbing season, another human, and twice the prior fee.
